1 Purpose, evidence and scope

Implement one shared connection and routing foundation for two uses in Spain: Sage software connects a business to its external private provider; later, the Sage private-platform proposition exchanges with public and other private platforms. Products and partners use the common access contract; selected adapters execute the supported external interfaces. Adding an operator role must not create a second connection registry, route engine or invoice history.

“Build once” describes reuse of shared behaviour. It does not mean one credential, endpoint, connection record or deployment can serve every role. A provider's customer interface and platform-interconnection interface may have different permissions, trust, registration and transport requirements. Qualify each separately and reuse an adapter only where its actual contract fits.

In scope: role-qualified connection profiles, separate registration observations and capability checks, controlled activation, deterministic route selection, adapter handoffs, suspension, migration qualification and historical dependencies. Open/gated expansion: operator interconnection, direct private exchange and a public bridge use the same model only after applicable evidence and approval. Connecting to providers first is a delivery sequence, not a technical prerequisite to operating a platform.

This compact architecture set extends the provider connector boundary discussed in SPEC-SEI-013. That source remains unchanged and remains the configured source for its stable Confluence page. These companions do not replace its Global API requirements. They describe Provider Connectors as consumers of the shared API and identify the Spain bindings still needing evidence. 1 Scope and boundary

A Sage product needs to exchange invoices through its customer's selected platform without implementing a separate provider integration in each product. The customer needs separately observable setup, delivery, retrieval and lifecycle results. The owning feature coordinates those results; a provider connector executes the qualified external operations.

Architecture direction confirmed by the user after architect discussion, 9 November 2026: products, authorised providers and Provider Connectors interact through the same Sage e-Invoicing API contract. Consumer roles have different operation permissions. The E-Invoice Service coordinates work; notifications can dispatch assigned work to a Provider Connector. The connector uses the selected external platform contract and submits source invoices, statuses and results through the shared API. CA-ARCH01/02. An exchange action is one separately tracked invoice delivery, public-copy submission or event report.

Provider Connector availability precedes customer setup. Provider Connector architecture belongs here; customer onboarding calls and outcomes remain in 037–040. Sending, receiving, lifecycle and offboarding retain their business rules in their feature folders.

Part 1 Feature Solution Summary

1 Purpose and reading route

This specification binds B2B Router to the shared Phase 2 connection, routing, invoice and recovery design. It defines what a Sage-managed B2B Router adapter must prove before pilot and production. It does not copy the shared platform design or make B2B Router concepts the Sage domain model.

Part 2 defines the logical behaviour. Part 3 defines interactions and data. Part 4 defines acceptance evidence and release gates. REF Source references identifies the exact source and its limits.

The labels in this document have these meanings:

2 Source authority and evidence update

The current public documentation is newer than the provider PRD review. It documents API version 2026-06-26, received-invoice webhook events, new import behaviour and revised environment guidance [B2BR-S02–S05]. This specification treats that version as an evidence candidate, not the selected build version. The selected version remains B2BR-Q01.

3 Scope and boundaries

In scope:

  • bind one B2B Router account scope to one authorised Sage connection scope;
  • qualify outbound, inbound, lifecycle, document retrieval and reconciliation separately;
  • execute an approved JSON-create or structured-file import strategy;
  • receive authenticated webhooks and recover missed observations through bounded reads;
  • preserve requested and actual provider transport/document-type facts;
  • keep route change, credential change, provider deregistration and historical release as separate actions;
  • preserve raw provider states and derive Sage lifecycle views under a versioned mapping.

Open for the first delivery cohort: contracted product/version, Spain registration and reachability, account/legal-entity cardinality, payload strategy, supported directions and formats, status provenance, idempotency, retention, service targets and exit sequence.

Out of scope: VeriFactu and other tax-report operations; provider commercial contracting; automatic route failover; per-invoice caller override; Private A → Private B customer switching; provider-side implementation; and direct B2B Router integration in each Sage ERP.

4 Terms, ownership and provider binding

5 Spain use and reuse qualification

Reuse of a proposed pattern is not proof that a deployed implementation is fit. Every candidate needs an actual build, contract, owner, gap record and test evidence before activation.

6 Process diagram and lifecycle

Editable Draw.io · PNG preview.

The flow starts when the shared platform supplies an authorised and version-bound action. B2BR-01 checks the provider binding. B2BR-02 freezes the selected provider operation and payload. B2BR-03 executes it once. A known response goes to B2BR-04. A possible external effect with no reliable result goes to B2BR-07 before any repeat. Webhooks accelerate observation through B2BR-05, while B2BR-06 performs independent bounded reconciliation. B2BR-08 preserves historical access after route change. Tax reporting stays outside the binding.

7 Material risks and decisions

The most material risks are wrong account scope, silent provider fallback, duplicate mutation, webhook gaps, overstatement of provider states, cross-environment key use, coupling to tax reporting and loss of historical access. Part 4 contains the blocking decisions. No implementation commitment should precede B2BR-Q01–Q04.

pages.title: Shared Error Handling and Operational Support
pages.source_excerpt:
1 Purpose and authority

Support, Enablement and Engineering need to find failed work, explain the evidenced cause and complete permitted recovery without routine engineering intervention. Customers need an accurate result and a safe next action. This document owns the proposed operational requirements common to the stage documents. The stage and functional specifications own their business decisions and recovery boundaries.

PRD107 already covers onboarding errors and recovery. PRD215 covers shared resilience. PRD225 covers observability, cases, safe actions and audit across the phases. The stakeholder note adds explicit search, historical investigation, version visibility and portal/bulk recovery needs. These are draft requirements for qualification, not evidence that a portal or action is implemented. OPS-S01–04 below identify their authority. Use the shared glossary.

2 Common operational requirements

Operation safety classes and reconciliation-first recovery remain in PRD225 — Operation safety classes. Retry budgets, numerical limits and escalation periods must be qualified per operation. The stakeholder's reported six-day retention is an unverified implementation concern. INT-ERR01's six-day support guidance is a different, code-specific source statement. Neither defines the required retention period, retry window or Spain reporting allowance. OPS-S03/04.

3 Stakeholder request coverage

4 Spain use, reuse and implementation evidence

Intended Spain use covers Phase 1 SPFE, enabled Phase 2 providers and the proposed Phase 3 Sage operator scope. These phase labels do not confirm delivery. Search, case history and guarded recovery are reusable design patterns. Existing support/case/search capabilities are implementation reuse candidates; Operations and Engineering must identify their actual builds, coverage, gaps and evidence. Actual implementation coverage is unknown.

Country and provider bindings select authority, regional configuration, exact codes, retry safety, deadlines and historical-route access. Spain identity, public-copy and reporting rules remain in the owning Spain specs. They must not become defaults for another country. Existing DTS is the preferred transformation candidate; SPEC049 qualifies its local mappings and recovery support. This document selects no new service, store or API.

5 Acceptance and open gates

Operations/Product own retention/search periods and portal/bulk release scope. Security owns recovery roles and bulk approval thresholds. API/Integration owners qualify identifiers, per-operation semantics and version evidence. Engineering/Operations own existing-tool coverage, alert thresholds and case ownership. Missing decisions block the dependent capability; they do not justify fabricated history or unsafe recovery. The checks above are required evidence, not executed product tests.
